subtopics.title: Year-End Adjustments and the Final Accounts

questions.question: The provision for bad debts stands at R14 000 but debtors of R240 000 justify only R12 000. The adjustment recorded is:
options: A decrease of R2 000 — only the movement in the provision touches the income statement
A new provision of R12 000 created from scratch
An increase of R2 000
Bad debts of R12 000 written off

questions.question: The correct order of the final accounts is:
options: Appropriation, then trading, then profit and loss
Trading, then profit and loss, then appropriation
Profit and loss, then appropriation, then trading
Trading, then appropriation, then profit and loss

questions.question: Net profit after tax is R394 200 and total dividends are R270 000. With opening retained income of R215 800, the closing retained income is:
options: R340 000 — the R124 200 retained for the year added to the opening balance

questions.question: Why must last year's accruals and prepayments be reversed at the start of the new year?
options: To reduce the tax charge
Because SARS requires it
To increase this year's profit
Otherwise the income and expenses concerned would be counted in two different years

questions.question: Sales are R3 600 000 and cost of sales R2 250 000. The gross profit and mark-up on cost are:
options: R1 350 000 and 60 percent
R1 350 000 and 37,5 percent
R2 250 000 and 60 percent
R1 350 000 and 40 percent

questions.question: Gross operating income of R1 440 000 less operating expenses of R840 000 gives:
options: Net profit after tax of R600 000
Operating profit of R600 000
Gross profit of R600 000
Retained income of R600 000

questions.question: Net profit before tax is R540 000 and income tax is 27 percent. Net profit after tax is:
Dividends do not appear among the operating expenses because:
options: They are too small to disclose
They are paid in cash
They are deducted from share capital
They are a distribution of profit after tax, shown in the retained income note, never above the profit line

subtopics.title: The Statement of Financial Position and Its Notes

questions.question: Ilanga's total assets are R3 750 000. Equity is R2 840 000 and the loan R500 000, so current liabilities must be:
options: R410 000 — the statement balances only if equity plus all liabilities equals total assets

questions.question: Shareholders for dividends of R150 000 represents:
options: The interim dividend paid in August
The final dividend declared on the last day but not yet paid — a current liability
Dividends received from investments
A long-term loan from shareholders

questions.question: The year's tax charge was R145 800 and provisional payments totalled R118 000. SARS income tax appears as:
options: A current asset of R27 800
A non-current liability of R145 800
A current liability of R27 800 — and had payments exceeded the charge, it would flip to a current asset
Nothing, because tax is closed off to appropriation

questions.question: The retained income note shows:
options: Authorised and issued shares
Cost and accumulated depreciation per asset class
The bank reconciliation
Opening balance, net profit after tax, interim and final dividends, and the closing balance

subtopics.title: The Cash Flow Statement and the Audit Report

questions.question: Depreciation is added back to net profit before tax in the cash flow statement because:
options: It reduced profit but no cash ever left the bank for it
It is a form of income
SARS refunds depreciation
It was paid in cash during the year

questions.question: Dividends paid in the cash flow statement equal R250 000 because they comprise:
options: This year's interim plus this year's final dividend
Last year's final dividend of R130 000 plus this year's interim of R120 000 — the newly declared final has moved no cash yet
Only the final dividend declared this year
All dividends declared over two years

questions.question: Operating activities gave R297 000 in, investing R470 000 out and financing R140 000 in. With opening cash of R163 000, closing cash is:
options: R130 000 — a net decrease of R33 000, matching the balance sheet's cash figure

questions.question: An unqualified audit opinion means:
options: The auditor was not qualified to audit the company
The statements are wrong in every respect
The auditor could not obtain enough evidence
The statements fairly present the company's position — a clean opinion with no reservations

questions.question: The statement of comprehensive income is like a video rather than a photograph because it:
options: Shows the whole year's trading compressed into one profit story
Is taken on the last day at midnight
Lists only what the business owns
Changes every time someone reads it

questions.question: The two sides of the statement of financial position both come to R3 750 000 because:
options: The accountant rounds them to match
Everything the company owns is claimed by somebody — owners or lenders
Assets always equal income
The auditor adjusts them until they agree

questions.question: A company can report a profit of R394 200 while its cash decreases because:
options: Profit is always false
The bank made an error
Profit counts sales when they happen and spreads asset costs over years, while cash counts only money actually moving
Tax takes all the profit

questions.question: The cash flow statement is described as a bridge because it:
options: Links the company to the JSE
Connects this year to next year
Joins the trading account to the appropriation account
Connects the profit story to what actually happened in the bank

questions.question: Stock rose by R40 000 during the year. In cash terms this is:
options: Cash out — money turned into boxes on the shelves
Cash in — stock is an asset
No effect on cash
Added back like depreciation

questions.question: Suppliers being owed R32 000 more than last year saves cash for now because:
options: The suppliers wrote off the debt
Goods were received but not yet paid for — the cash is still in the tin
It reduces cost of sales
Interest is earned on amounts owed

questions.question: The R450 000 spent on new equipment belongs in:
options: Operating activities
Financing activities
Investing activities — cash spent on the company's future capacity
The appropriation account

questions.question: The completed cash flow statement must end on:
options: Net profit after tax
Retained income
Total assets
The closing cash balance of R130 000 — exactly the cash figure on the statement of financial position

questions.question: An audit exists because the directors preparing the statements are reporting on:
options: Their own performance — like a learner marking their own examination
The shareholders' personal finances
SARS collections
The JSE's trading systems

questions.question: A qualified opinion, in the roadworthy picture, means:
options: The taxi passed with no reservations
Roadworthy except for listed matters — the statements are fair except for specific issues the auditor names
The examiner refused to test the taxi
The taxi failed completely

questions.question: The audit report is addressed to the shareholders because:
options: Shareholders pay the auditor personally
Directors are not allowed to read it
The auditor works for the owners, checking the managers — never the other way round
The law requires all letters to go to shareholders

questions.question: An auditor holding shares in the client company is a problem because:
options: Auditors earn too much already
It increases the audit fee
Shareholders may not own shares
Independence is compromised — the auditor has a personal reason to soften the verdict that everyone downstream trusts
